minutes.headline: Finance Committee agreed the Feb–March town meeting schedule to send to the interim town manager; school budget set for March 6.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed the interim town manager's deadlines for getting to Town Meeting and a proposed Thursday schedule of department hearings, and voted to tell him it agrees. It heard that health insurance estimates may run high, that the superintendent is retiring at year end, and an update on the town manager search. A resident raised cemetery commission spending, and the January 23 meeting was effectively dropped unless something comes up.

public_comment.topic: Alleged misuse of the cemetery commission's sale-of-lots account, including a revote to buy a records software license; says he will propose a warrant article to rein in the use of that money and asked the committee's support.

budget_items.what_was_said: A resident said the commission revoted spending on a vital-records software license and cited earlier alleged misuse; he referred to the money the town allots the commission.
The interim town manager has no rate estimates yet but said market trends are high and the town's poor expense ratio puts it at the top; he anticipates about this figure as a guess.
The district is no longer in the hold harmless category, and the chair does not expect a windfall.
The chair said a policy and procedure is needed to get grant writing help, since staff and commissioners are strapped; Caesar will follow up with the interim town manager.
A member reported a former student gave a scholarship for athletics use.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill fire alarms, doors, truck and plow
budget_items.what_was_said: The finance director arranged replacement of fire alarms at Turkey Hill; new doors are expensive and undecided; a new truck and plow were ordered.

decisions.decision: Key dates discussed: committee report to town manager due March 31, votes by March 20, public hearing March 13 with ledger notice 10 days prior, draft budget and warrant February 13.
One out-of-cycle meeting (February 25) will be needed; the chair will verify room availability.
School department hearing set for March 6; the superintendent said she would endeavor to meet that date.
Select board chair Caesar will follow up with the interim town manager on a process for grant writing services.
The January 23 meeting will be held only if something pressing comes up; otherwise skipped, next meeting February 13.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted by roll call to tell the interim town manager it agrees with his Town Meeting timeline and the proposed department hearing schedule; the result was not stated.
Key dates discussed: draft budget and warrant February 13, public hearing March 13, committee votes by March 20, committee report to the town manager March 31.
The school department hearing is set for March 6; the superintendent said she would endeavor to meet that date, and one out-of-cycle meeting on February 25 will be needed.
The interim town manager has no health insurance rate estimates yet but said market trends are high; the superintendent's year-end retirement was announced.
The January 23 meeting will be held only if something pressing comes up; otherwise the next meeting is February 13.

why_it_matters: The dates set here decide when the school and town budgets get a hearing and when a resident can speak before the committee votes and Town Meeting.
Health insurance is a cost the town does not yet have a figure for, so the FY26 budget could change once rates arrive.
A resident said he will propose a warrant article on cemetery commission spending, which would be a vote residents may be asked to take at Town Meeting.
